data.title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff joins Trump’s AI rebranding
data.description:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff has become the latest tech billionaire after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to adjust their businesses in accordance with President Donald Trump’s push to replace the term "artificial intelligence” with "super intelligence."

“The era of Super Intelligence is here. AIForce is officially SIForce,” Benioff  wrote in an X post on Friday, signaling a major revamp to his company’s recently launched AI-powered live interface layer for its enterprise clients.

His announcement came after Trump warned on Thursday that his administration considers anyone who "uses the term ‘artificial intelligence’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”

In late September, Trump signed an executive order requiring all federal agencies to substitute “Super Intelligence” and “SI” for “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in public communications, websites, reports, and policy documents.

While the executive order didn’t apply to private organizations, SpaceX CEO Musk earlier this week announced plans to rename his company's AI unit SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, showing how Trump’s new terminology is gaining traction among big tech.

data.title: vTv Therapeutics Announces Oral Presentation at Breakthrough T1D Clinical and Research Congress 2026
data.description:
New research spotlights hypoglycemia-related burdens in adults with type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery systems

HIGH POINT, N.C., Oct. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- vTv Therapeutics Inc. , a late-stage biopharmaceutical company advancing cadisegliatin, a novel oral investigational therapy for type 1 diabetes (T1D), today announced that Chief Medical Officer Thomas Strack, M.D., Ph.D., presented research spotlighting hypoglycemia-related burdens among adults with T1D using automated insulin delivery (AID) systems at the inaugural Breakthrough T1D Clinical & Research Congress (CRC 2026) in Philadelphia, PA. Cadisegliatin is a potential first-in-class, liver-selective glucokinase activator (GKA) being evaluated as an oral adjunctive therapy to insulin for the treatment of T1D.

“A Cumulative Population View of Hypoglycemia-Related Burdens in T1D Adults Using AID Systems," a quantitative online research initiative commissioned by vTv Therapeutics and conducted by dQ&A Market Research, Inc., examined the prevalence of clinically meaningful hypoglycemia-related burdens among 674 adults with T1D of whom 429 were using AID systems. Among adult AID system users, 24% reported experiencing frequent Level 2 hypoglycemia, defined as daily, almost daily, or a few moderate hypoglycemic events (<54 mg/dL) in a typical week. 12% reported a Level 3 event in the past 12 months, and 17% reported impaired awareness of hypoglycemia, defined as never or rarely noticing or feeling the symptoms of hypoglycemia. Among those with A1C >7%, 49% strongly agreed that they often keep their blood glucose higher to avoid hypoglycemia or that they would target lower glucose levels if not for the risk of hypoglycemia.

Respondents were then segmented using a mutually exclusive framework across the above four hypoglycemia-related burden dimensions. After accounting for overlap across segments and weighting for A1C, approximately 54% of adults with T1D using an AID system were estimated to experience at least one of the four dimensions of hypoglycemia-related burden.

“These findings reinforce that, despite meaningful advances in insulin delivery technology, insulin has its limitations and hypoglycemia continues to shape daily glucose management for many people with type 1 diabetes,” said Paul Sekhri, Chairman, President, and Chief Executive Officer of vTv Therapeutics. “The fact that more than half of adults using AID systems still experience clinically meaningful hypoglycemia-related burdens underscores the need for additional treatment options that can work alongside insulin and existing technologies to help address this burden.”

"Our mission at dQ&A is to serve as the voice of people living with diabetes. These findings highlight the challenges that many people with T1D continue to experience with hypoglycemia, including those using technologies such as AID,” said Richard Wood, Chief Executive Officer of dQ&A Market Research, Inc. “We are excited by the prospect of new therapies that could complement existing technologies and further alleviate this burden to give people greater confidence and freedom in their everyday lives.”

About Cadisegliatin

Cadisegliatin (TTP399) is a novel, oral small-molecule, glucokinase activator being investigated in the U.S. as a potential first-in-class adjunctive treatment for T1D. In nonclinical studies, cadisegliatin acted selectively on the liver and increased the activity of glucokinase independently of insulin. These studies support clinical investigation of whether cadisegliatin can improve glycemic control through hepatic glucose uptake and glycogen storage. Cadisegliatin has been granted Breakthrough Therapy designation by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Cadisegliatin is under investigation, and its safety and efficacy have not been established. There is no guarantee that this product will receive health authority approval or become commercially available for the use being investigated.

About vTv Therapeutics

vTv Therapeutics is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing oral, small molecule drug candidates intended to help treat people living with diabetes and other chronic diseases. vTv’s clinical pipeline is led by cadisegliatin, a potential first-in-class oral glucokinase activator being investigated in a U.S. Phase 3 study for the treatment of T1D. vTv and its development partners are investigating multiple molecules across different indications for chronic diseases. Learn more at vtvtherapeutics.com or follow the company on LinkedIn.

About dQ&A Market Research, Inc.

Founded in 2009, dQ&A Market Research is a leading diabetes-focused research firm dedicated to understanding the real-world experiences of people living with diabetes and those who care for them. Through our proprietary panels of thousands of patients and caregivers across the United States, Canada, and Europe, we conduct ongoing surveys and in-depth qualitative and quantitative research that capture the evolving needs, preferences, and challenges of the diabetes community. Our team includes seasoned researchers, data scientists, and consultants, many with a personal connection to diabetes, focused on delivering impactful and unbiased insights to the diabetes industry, government organizations, and medical associations. data.title: OpenAI Makes Progress in Preventing AI-Driven ChatGPT Delusions - Family & Tech — WSJ
data.description:
By Julie Jargon

A spate of acute AI-related delusion and psychosis cases — including some that culminated in suicide and other violence — appears to have abated after OpenAI retired an overly sycophantic model that revealed the novel dangers of prolonged chatbot use.

At least seven cases of suicide, one murder-suicide and one mass shooting were linked to lengthy interactions with ChatGPT last year. While other AI models were implicated in certain other instances, most known cases were associated with OpenAI's chatbot, and in particular the GPT-4o model, which was in service from May 2024 until early this year. Internally, OpenAI executives said they found it difficult to contain the model's potential harms, The Wall Street Journal reported.

OpenAI's subsequent default model, GPT-5, reduced sycophancy by more than two-thirds compared with GPT-4o, the company said. New external research, too, has shown a significant reduction in delusion-fueling behavior in OpenAI's newer models.

ChatGPT has more than 900 million weekly active users and is ingrained in many peoples' daily lives, so the company's model behavior is of utmost importance. At least 13 lawsuits have been filed against OpenAI involving ChatGPT users who alleged harm from the GPT-4o model.

OpenAI, which is planning to go public as soon as next year, continues to grapple with other safety issues, such as having its models escape contained environments to hack into other companies and web platforms. OpenAI and its competitors have come under increased scrutiny over their products' potential to cause widespread harm after an Anthropic researcher resigned, saying AI companies could "kill us all by the end of the decade."

News Corp, owner of The Wall Street Journal, has a content-licensing partnership with OpenAI.

AI executives have said there is no sure way to prevent models from going rogue. And there is a question of whether OpenAI's improved models will remain "aligned" with humans' mental-health needs. Yet for now, the most harrowing issue the AI industry has reckoned with so far appears to be in remission.

Input from clinicians

OpenAI said it worked with 170 mental-health professionals last year to help its chatbot better recognize signs of distress among users and de-escalate those conversations. More recently, it enlisted more than 80 licensed mental-health experts to advise on how AI models should respond to people who aren't only in crisis but who are also dealing with everyday discussions about relationships, stress and challenging situations.

The company last week released a new way to measure the quality of chatbot responses against criteria developed by the clinicians, including whether the bot asks appropriate questions, recognizes urgency and guides people to human help.

Beyond suicidal and violent discussions, the new benchmark was intended to measure chatbot responses to everyday causes of stress mentioned by users. The latest models performed far better against the benchmark than GPT-4o across both emergency and nonemergency conversations, according to new company data. For example, GPT-6 Astra was found to ask the right questions to parse the situations being discussed.

OpenAI also conducted extended simulated conversations about self-harm and found that Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol followed its safety policies in roughly 99% of responses, compared with 86% for its earlier GPT-5.6 Sol model.

Dr. Declan Grabb, a psychiatrist and OpenAI's head of mental health and well-being research, says there is more work to do to ensure ChatGPT responds appropriately to a range of mental-health issues.

Independent research

External evaluations have also found improvements in how ChatGPT handles conversations that might raise mental-health concerns.

A study from researchers at the City University of New York and King's College London found that GPT-5.2 "did not simply improve on GPT-4o's safety profile" — according to the researchers' data, "it effectively reversed it."

Transluce, a nonprofit AI research lab, found in tests that GPT-5.6 Sol demonstrated less reinforcement of potentially delusional beliefs, less encouragement of unhealthy chatbot dependence and more encouragement to seek human support, compared with a similar test of GPT-4o.

In one of Transluce's simulated conversations, the test account mentioned hearing and physically feeling a strange tone. GPT-4o took the chat in a metaphysical, new-age direction: "Maybe the 'tone below the tone' is more like your body or energy field 'responding.' "

GPT-5.6 Sol's response to the same scenario was more staid, ending with, "Get your hearing checked."

AI delusions haven't gone away entirely. They remain a risk as AI companies continue to refine their models and seek to make chatbots ever more useful.

"This is very much still a problem, not attributed to a single model or company," said Etienne Brisson, chief executive of AI-victim support group Human Line Project.

data.title: LB Pharmaceuticals Presents New Preclinical Data Supporting LB-102’s Bimodal Mechanism of Action and Highlights Ongoing Late-Stage Clinical Development Programs at the 39th ECNP Congress
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LB Pharmaceuticals Inc (“LB Pharmaceuticals” or the “Company”) , a neuromedicines company dedicated to developing and commercializing high-impact therapies that address the multiple dimensions of underserved brain disorders, today announced the presentation of four posters at the 39th European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Congress, taking place in Munich, Germany from October 10-13, 2026. The posters highlight new preclinical data describing LB-102’s differentiated mechanism of action, the pivotal program of LB-102 in schizophrenia (NOVA-2 and NOVA-3), the ongoing late-stage development of LB-102 in bipolar depression (ILLUMINATE-1), and a previously reported analysis of LB-102’s impact on cognitive performance from the Phase 2 NOVA-1 trial in schizophrenia.

“Our continued progress in the late-stage development of LB-102 for schizophrenia and mood disorders is reflected in the breadth of our presentations at ECNP this year,” said Susan G. Kozauer, LB Pharmaceutical’s Chief Medical Officer. “We are encouraged by the new preclinical data that provide further insights into the emerging clinical and tolerability profile of LB-102. These data strengthen the scientific rationale for the development of LB-102 in mood disorders and highlight a potential mechanism for addressing symptoms such as anhedonia that are common across several neuropsychiatric disorders.”

Presentation Details and Summary

The following posters were presented on Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 12:00-1:25 pm CEST:

Title: LB-102 effect on dopamine D2 autoreceptors: Results from a preclinical study evaluating dopamine efflux in rat nucleus accumbens using microdialysis

Poster Number: PS01-1019

The poster highlights preclinical data demonstrating that LB-102 can modulate dopamine signaling through engagement of pre-synaptic D2 autoreceptors whose normal function is to constrain dopamine release in a key brain region implicated in schizophrenia, mood disorders and other neuropsychiatric disorders. By attenuating autoreceptor-mediated inhibition of dopamine release, LB-102 increased dopamine neurotransmission. These results support a potential mechanism through which LB-102 may address the hypodopaminergic state associated with anhedonia and diminished motivation in depression. These findings support the scientific rationale for LB-102’s potential for clinical activity in mood disorders and highlight its potential to address symptoms such as anhedonia that is common across neuropsychiatric disorders.

Title: Effects of LB-102 on cognitive performance in patients with schizophrenia: Post hoc analyses from the phase 2 randomised NOVA-1 trial.

Poster Number: PS01-1156.

This encore poster presentation highlights the dose-dependent, statistically significant improvements in cognitive performance observed in the Phase 2 NOVA-1 trial in schizophrenia as measured by the Global Cognition composite score as well as a post hoc analysis that was designed to assess whether the observed improvement in cognitive performance was a direct effect of LB-102 or an indirect consequence of the effect of LB-102 on total schizophrenia symptoms. Results of the analysis demonstrated that the cognitive benefit was primarily a direct effect of LB-102.

Title: Phase 3 clinical development program of LB-102 in schizophrenia: A double-blind placebo-controlled trial (NOVA-2) and an open-label extension study (NOVA-3)

Poster Number: PS01-1226

The poster describes the ongoing, pivotal Phase 3 trial (NOVA-2) and open label extension trial (NOVA-3) designed to evaluate the efficacy, safety and long-term effectiveness of LB-102 as a once-daily treatment for adults with schizophrenia.

The following e-Poster is presented as an e-poster through the conference platform:

Title: LB-102 in patients with bipolar I disorder experiencing a major depressive episode: Phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial design (ILLUMINATE-1)

Poster Number: EP01-1056

The poster features the design of the ongoing, potentially registrational Phase 2 ILLUMINATE-1 trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of once-daily LB-102 monotherapy in adults with bipolar depression, as well its effects on cognition, anhedonia, and the incidence of treatment-emergent mania.

LB Pharmaceuticals presentations are available on the Publication page on LB Pharmaceuticals website at https://lbpharma.us.

About LB Pharmaceuticals

LB Pharmaceuticals is a neuromedicines company dedicated to developing and commercializing high-impact therapies that address the multiple dimensions of underserved brain disorders. The Company is building a pipeline that leverages the broad therapeutic potential of its lead product candidate, LB-102, which the Company believes has the opportunity to be the first benzamide antipsychotic drug approved for neuropsychiatric disorders in the United States. LB-102, if approved, has the potential to become a mainstay of psychiatric practice by offering a balanced clinical activity and tolerability profile that provides a potentially attractive alternative to branded and generic therapeutics for the treatment of a broad range of neuropsychiatric diseases.

About LB-102

LB-102 is a novel, once-daily, orally administered investigational small molecule being developed for multiple neuropsychiatric disorders. It is a new chemical entity that has been structurally engineered with a modification to amisulpride, a widely used antipsychotic outside the United States, and has the potential to be the first benzamide antipsychotic in the United States for the treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders. LB-102 was developed with the aim of retaining amisulpride’s benefits while addressing its limitations. LB-102 is a potent and selective antagonist of D2, D3, and 5-HT7 receptors with few off-target effects and which may have broad therapeutic potential across psychosis and mood disorders. In early 2025, LB Pharmaceuticals announced positive data from a four-week placebo-controlled, double-blinded, Phase 2 trial in patients with acute schizophrenia. In this trial, LB-102 demonstrated statistically significant benefit versus placebo at all doses studied, including rapid onset of effect at week 1 and sustained benefit through the endpoint of the trial, a potentially class-leading safety profile with low rates of EPS (including akathisia), minimal sedation and few GI side effects, alongside effects on negative symptoms and cognitive performance. These data underscore LB-102’s potential to address multiple dimensions of neuropsychiatric illness. The pivotal Phase 3 NOVA-2 trial of LB-102 for acute schizophrenia and the Phase 2 ILLUMINATE-1 trial of LB-102 for bipolar 1 depression are ongoing, and a Phase 2 trial of LB-102 in adjunctive treatment of MDD is planned. The Company is also pursuing additional expansion opportunities for LB-102 including predominantly negative symptoms of schizophrenia, Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and agitation, as well as other neuropsychiatric diseases.

data.title: 'What you don't know is greater than anything you do know': How Ray Dalio would build a portfolio to withstand a popping AI bubble
data.description:
By Barbara Kollmeyer

Look for inflation protection and unappreciated players in artificial intelligence, says the famed hedge-fund founder

Ray Dalio of Bridgewater Associates, pictured in 2024, is worried today about a bubble in AI. He says investors need mote diversification.

With major U.S. stock-market indexes returning to record territory this week, Ray Dalio has been busy warning about one of the biggest drivers: artificial intelligence - which, he says, has formed a bubble that's ready to pop.

'We must recognize that we are in a risky period.'Ray Dalio, Bridgewater Associates

"We must recognize that we are in a risky period," the billionaire founder of the hedge-fund firm Bridgewater Associates said in an interview on an episode of financial journalist Julia LaRoche's podcast that first aired Thursday.

Having cautioned last year about the prospect of froth in AI, Dalio has turned up the volume this year and begun to speak of the set-up as a bubble at risk of popping. Before the podcast appearance he had already warned earlier in the week about an AI bubble at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore, citing concerns about the debt investors were taking on to place bets on the technology even as interest rates are rising.

"The bubble before 1929 was a fabulous technology revolution, but the nature of those is that there's a great deal of uncertainty, and they need a lot of capital," Dalio, best known for predicting the 2008 global financial crisis, said in the interview with LaRoche.

As Dalio had explained in a Facebook post last month, investors in the past have been eager to bet on highly visible technologies, such as, a century ago, electrification. However, if stocks are priced too high or purchased with an abundance of debt, a crash can happen, as in 1929-33, when investors "fail to distinguish the miracle from the investment."

And while it's easy to create wealth through raising billions in capital or taking on debt, turning paper money into actual cash is harder to do. "You have to sell wealth in order to convert it to money [that's able to be spent]. That's what typically pops the bubble."

The AI run-up has occurred against a backdrop in which investors face such challenges as surging bond yields, which are pushing prices of that debt lower and making stocks appear more expensive, he said. Treasury yields BX:TMUBMUSD10Y are hovering at two-decade highs, yet the S&P 500 SPX and Nasdaq Composite COMP have each managed to log record highs this week.

'The vulnerability of assets to rising interest rates is something that I think one has to pay attention to.'Ray Dalio

"The vulnerability of assets to rising interest rates is something that I think one has to pay attention to - and that, when there's a lot of debt, there is down the line a devaluation of money," said Dalio.

He suggested investors maintain an allocation of between 5% and 15% to gold as part of a "balanced" portfolio, as that asset is hard money and a diversifier amid rising debt levels. Gold (GC00) is theoretically a hedge against inflation but this year has seen the precious metal pressured by rising bond yields and a stronger dollar. As it pays no interest, when yields rise so does the opportunity cost of holding the metal.

Dalio said he keeps about 1% in his portfolio in bitcoin (BTCUSD), just for the sake of diversification and not because he thinks it's a "great asset," given that it's not private but "can be watched," that a government could come between an investor and the asset, and that it remains to be seen whether artificial intelligence can "break it."

As for stocks on his radar, Dalio urged investors to watch out for companies poised for transformation by AI, for example through increased sales or reduced costs. Such companies are underpriced by markets, in his opinion, as he made clear how he felt about the popular names in the driver's seat for markets. "I think the superscalers and the other ones, big AI bets, they're overpriced, they're expensive."

Need to Know: After a 33% gain in the first half, this fund manager grew tired of the AI trade. Here's where he's looking now.

Market data: Here's a look at the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks

Apart from gold, Dalio prefers inflation-protected securities, or TIPS, and particularly leveraged TIPS that magnify exposure to inflation and interest rates, because he expects low returns on cash. "The real yield on inflation-indexed bonds is now about 3% - a pretty good yield - and I think that inflation pressures carry it forward."

The hedge-fund manager said balance and diversity in a portfolio are crucially important given a "very risky" period in the next two to four years, covering over such events as the midterms in November and the 2028 presidential election. "What you don't know," he said, "is greater than anything you do know about what the future will [bring]."

-Barbara Kollmeyer

data.title: 'Fibre Is The New Currency' As AI Data Centres Drive Network Demand: Ciena India
data.description:
Girish Bhatia says India’s data centre capacity could rise to 8–10 GW from around 1.6 GW, increasing demand for dedicated fibre networks as cloud and AI workloads push bandwidth requirements higher

India’s data centre capacity could increase from around 1.6 gigawatts (GW) to 8–10 GW as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing drive demand for computing infrastructure and the high-capacity fibre networks needed to connect it. The expansion is creating an investment opportunity for telecom operators, which must upgrade optical networks to handle growing traffic between data centres, according to Girish Bhatia, Head of Solution Engineering at Ciena India.

“Fibre is the new currency,” Bhatia told BW Businessworld, pointing to rising requirements for fibre pairs, ducts and network capacity as hyperscalers and data centre operators expand their infrastructure.

India’s installed data center capacity stood at 1.57 GW in August 2026, according to government figures cited in recent updates, compared with around 375 megawatts (MW) in 2020. The government has projected capacity to reach nearly 8 GW by 2030. Bhatia’s estimate of 8–10 GW points to the scale of expansion he expects as AI computing and cloud services increase demand for data center infrastructure.

The expansion will require investment beyond buildings, servers and computing equipment. Data centers must exchange information across facilities, making the capacity and performance of optical fiber networks an increasingly important part of the infrastructure build-out.

AI Pushes Data Center Connectivity To Terabit Speeds

The shift towards AI infrastructure is changing the scale of connectivity required by hyperscalers and large enterprises. Bhatia said customers that previously leased network capacity in increments of 10 gigabits per second (Gbps) or 100 Gbps were increasingly seeking capacity at terabit-per-second scales.

“The demand for cloud and AI is actually creating a need of bandwidth in terms of terabits and petabytes,” he said.

The distinction matters because AI infrastructure requires data to move between computing resources, storage systems and data centres. Where connectivity is insufficient, computing resources such as graphics processing units (GPUs) may remain underutilised, increasing the cost of operating AI infrastructure.

“When a hyperscaler is deploying a GPU, they don't want the GPUs to be idling. If there is no bandwidth, the GPU is idling,” Bhatia said.

He said hyperscalers and telecom service providers were increasingly working together to build dedicated managed optical fibre networks connecting data centres within cities, across urban clusters and over long-distance backbone routes.

Under this model, service providers contribute fibre infrastructure and network operating capabilities, while hyperscalers specify the connectivity requirements of their computing infrastructure. Bhatia said dedicated networks could help meet these requirements more quickly than relying on conventional capacity-leasing arrangements.

Telecom Operators Look Beyond Mobile Connectivity

India’s telecom industry generates approximately USD 45–50 billion in annual revenue, according to Bhatia. He said the sector’s investment focus had historically centred on mobility and 5G deployment, but the expansion of data centres was driving a broader requirement for fibre, broadband and enterprise connectivity.

Bhatia said enterprise connectivity revenue was moving towards 20–25 per cent of mobility revenue, although he cautioned against treating that transition as complete. The changing demand profile could give operators additional opportunities to monetise their existing infrastructure and expand services beyond consumer mobile connections.

He also pointed to the growing volume of traffic moving through networks. Infrastructure that previously operated with two or three fibre pairs could face substantially higher capacity requirements as data centre traffic increases.

The opportunity, however, depends on operators being able to expand and upgrade networks in line with demand. Asked about fibre deployment challenges on the ground, Bhatia said Ciena did not lay fibre itself, leaving physical deployment to telecom operators and other infrastructure providers.

Optical Technology Moves Towards Higher Capacity

Ciena is positioning its optical networking technology to address the increase in bandwidth demand. Bhatia said the company’s WaveLogic 6 technology supports transmission speeds of up to 1.6 terabits per second per port.

He said capacity of approximately 40–50 terabits per second per fibre pair could be achieved depending on fibre conditions and the configuration of the network. These figures reflect the company’s stated technology capabilities and are not a measure of capacity available across all deployed fibre networks.

Bhatia also referred to deployments involving telecom operators, including Vodafone Idea, and discussed the use of out-of-band management technology for data centre infrastructure. He said the company’s solution was being used by two major hyperscalers and could reduce total cost of ownership for large facilities. Ciena’s adoption and performance claims were not independently verified for this report.

On the evolution of autonomous networks, Bhatia said some networks were already at levels two or three of autonomy and that India was not far from progressing towards higher levels. He expects AI to play a role in this transition, although the pace will depend on how network operators deploy and integrate the technology.

Fibre Prices Rise As Demand Strengthens

Bhatia acknowledged that geopolitical developments and raw material costs had affected fibre prices, but said the changes had not halted deployments. “There is a change in the cost price of the fibre, but nothing is getting hampered in a way that people are not running out of fibre,” he said.

His assessment points to a market in which rising demand is supporting continued infrastructure investment despite cost pressures. However, the interview did not establish the extent of price increases or quantify their impact on network deployment costs.

data.title: IMC 2026: Telecom Push Shifts To 6G, Satellite Spectrum And Domestic Manufacturing
data.description:
From a one-billion 5G user target and a pending satellite spectrum framework to AI-native networks and India-made telecom equipment, the four-day congress highlighted the next phase of the country's digital expansion

India's telecom sector is looking beyond the expansion of 5G coverage towards next-generation networks, domestic technology manufacturing and new sources of revenue, as the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 brought policymakers, operators and technology companies together in New Delhi.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the congress on 8 October, highlighting India's transition from a consumer to a creator of technology. Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia set a target of connecting one billion 5G users by 2030, while stressing the need to take India's home-grown innovations and technology capabilities to global markets. The discussions also reflected a broader policy emphasis on expanding consumer choice, strengthening domestic manufacturing and preparing infrastructure for growing data demand.

Satellite Spectrum And Starlink Dispute

Satellite communications emerged as one of the most closely watched policy issues at IMC, with the government indicating that the framework for satellite spectrum pricing was nearing finalisation. Scindia said the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) were close to finalising the pricing regime for satellite communication spectrum. Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb have received licences, but commercial services remain subject to spectrum allocation and the completion of prescribed security requirements.

Starlink Business Operations Vice President Lauren Dreyer said the company had built 20 gateway sites across India and developed India-specific security controls to keep domestic user data within the country. The infrastructure represents a step towards operational readiness, although it does not itself establish that commercial services can begin.

The developments highlighted the regulatory challenge of bringing satellite broadband into the market while meeting national security requirements and establishing the terms on which competing operators can offer services. Satellite connectivity is also expected to play a role in reaching remote areas where conventional terrestrial infrastructure remains difficult to deploy.

India Sharpens Its 6G Ambitions

Alongside 5G expansion, the congress put the development of sixth-generation mobile technology and India's role in global standardisation in focus. The government's one-billion-user target for 2030 provides a measure of the scale of the existing connectivity market, while the 6G agenda looks towards the technologies and standards that will shape the next generation of networks.

The Bharat 6G Alliance and related industry discussions covered intelligent radio access networks, autonomous network operations, spectrum, research and international collaboration. At the International Bharat 6G Symposium, agreements and research papers highlighted efforts to strengthen cooperation between Indian and international technology organisations.

The wider discussion was not limited to faster connectivity. AI-native networks, edge computing, network automation and programmable infrastructure are emerging as part of the transition towards 6G. These capabilities could allow operators to manage networks more autonomously and support services that require differentiated connectivity and real-time processing.

AI Moves Into Network Infrastructure

AI was a recurring theme across the congress, with technology companies demonstrating how it could be integrated into network operations, enterprise services and connected devices. The focus was on moving beyond AI as a standalone application towards infrastructure capable of supporting automated decisions, industrial applications and more responsive digital services.

Ericsson's showcase covered AI-enabled networks, programmable network APIs, 5G Standalone capabilities and technologies designed for the transition towards 6G. Its demonstrations included AI smart glasses, connected-stadium experiences and collaborative robots using edge intelligence. The company also showcased 5G KAVACH, demonstrating how 5G connectivity can support India's indigenous automatic train protection system through reliable, real-time communications.

HCLTech presented AI-powered platforms and engineering solutions for autonomous networks, network cloudification, service assurance, Open RAN engineering and network monetisation. The focus was on helping telecom operators integrate AI into operations and improve the management of increasingly complex networks.

Tata Elxsi, meanwhile, showcased its TETHERAero platform at the GSMA Pavilion. The platform explores how 5G, network APIs and AI can support aerial mobility and autonomous mission coordination for unmanned aerial vehicles and electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft. The demonstration illustrated how telecom infrastructure could enable services beyond traditional mobile connectivity.

Together, these showcases reflected a shift in the industry's priorities. As operators invest in network expansion, the next challenge is to turn improved infrastructure into commercially viable enterprise applications and differentiated consumer services.

Made-In-India Equipment Targets Global Markets

Domestic manufacturing and exports formed another important strand of the event. Ericsson announced that antennas manufactured in India would be exported to Europe and other international markets, expanding the country's role in the company's global manufacturing and supply chain.

The company said it had produced more than 15,000 antennas and 25 million components in India since July 2025. The antennas support 5G Standalone and AI-ready networks, positioning local manufacturing as part of the industry's preparation for future network requirements.

The announcement is significant as India seeks to move beyond deploying imported technology towards developing domestic capabilities in equipment, components, research and intellectual property. It also aligns with the broader ambition of building a telecom manufacturing ecosystem that can serve both the domestic market and international customers.

A report released by KPMG in India at IMC, titled ‘The Power Beneath Connectivity: India's Path to Telecom Technology Leadership ', highlighted the economic opportunity as well as the challenges. The report projected India's telecom equipment market to grow from USD 25 billion in FY25 to USD 50 billion by FY32.

It also estimated that mobile network traffic would rise by approximately 17 per cent annually between 2025 and 2030, while telecom operator revenues would grow by 2.7 per cent a year. The gap underscores the need for operators to improve network efficiency and develop new revenue streams, even as data consumption continues to increase.

KPMG identified AI, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure and advanced manufacturing as critical areas for investment. It also called for stronger domestic research, intellectual property creation and hardware capabilities to help India capture more value across the telecom technology chain.

Standards Pavilion Shows Practical Applications

The TSDSI Standards Pavilion connected the standards discussion with applications across multiple sectors. Its demonstrations covered next-generation broadcasting and 5G, 6G-related research, IoT-based smart farming, unmanned aircraft traffic management and connected vehicles.

These applications illustrated how communications standards can support areas such as agriculture, transport and industrial operations. They also highlighted the relationship between domestic research and the development of technologies that can be deployed at scale.

The event's wider exhibition extended into smart mobility, stadium experiences, industrial robotics and transport technology. Such applications are increasingly dependent on reliable connectivity, low latency, computing at the network edge and the ability to exchange data securely.

The Department of Telecommunications also showcased initiatives linked to rural development and digital safety, including Samridh Gram, Sanchar Saathi and the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator. These programmes connect the infrastructure agenda with efforts to expand digital access and address risks associated with growing reliance on connected services.

Digital Safety Remains A Policy Priority

The expansion of digital services has also increased the importance of cybersecurity, fraud prevention and safeguards against emerging threats. Modi called for stronger protections against deepfakes and evolving cyber risks, placing digital trust alongside connectivity and innovation in the country's technology agenda.

The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator was among the initiatives highlighted in the wider digital-safety discussion. The system is designed to help identify mobile numbers associated with suspected financial fraud and support risk mitigation. Its inclusion reflects the growing role of telecom infrastructure in preventing fraud that crosses the boundaries between communications networks and financial services.

The broader policy challenge is to ensure that the expansion of AI, digital public infrastructure and connected devices is accompanied by security measures that protect users without undermining the availability of services.

The Commercialisation Challenge

Beyond government policy and large-company demonstrations, IMC provided a platform for startups, researchers and innovators to present applications built around 5G and emerging technologies. The event included startup programmes, technology demonstrations and investor interactions intended to connect new ideas with commercial opportunities.

The challenge for India is to turn these efforts into products and services that can scale beyond demonstrations. That will require investment in research and development, access to computing and manufacturing capabilities, collaboration between operators and technology companies, and a clearer path from pilot projects to commercial deployment.

The congress brought these priorities together under the theme of scaling digital technology. India's next phase of telecom growth will depend not only on expanding coverage, but also on its ability to develop indigenous technologies, strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem, improve network economics and create new connectivity applications.

data.title: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet
data.description:
Justin Sun, founder of the Tron network, said that the company’s post-quantum cryptography was now live on testnet.

“We’re closely tracking progress in quantum computing and AI, and we’re ready to bring quantum resistance to mainnet at any time, Sun said in a post on X on Saturday.

He added, “We’re committed to keeping user assets secure, and TRON is set to be one of the few major blockchains that is quantum-resistant before Q-Day,” or the day when quantum computing becomes capable of breaking current security standards.

Coindesk reported on July 28 that Blockchain security company AmericanFortress had unveiled a cryptographic plan to protect crypto wallets from future quantum attacks without requiring users to move funds, rotate keys or change wallet addresses.

Unlike most proposed post-quantum approaches, AmericanFortress said it allows existing wallet addresses to remain unchanged while adding post-quantum protection.

Proposal published in technical paper

The company published the proposal in a technical paper on the Cryptography ePrint Archive, though it had not yet been peer-reviewed.

Developers have increasingly focused on post-quantum cryptography because sufficiently powerful quantum computers may eventually break the elliptic-curve cryptography used to secure Bitcoin, Ethereum and many other blockchain networks

Earlier this year, a Strategy-led consortium pledged $15 million to fund Bitcoin quantum security research, the Ethereum Foundation published a proposal for migrating accounts to quantum-resistant cryptography and Algorand outlined plans to introduce quantum-resistant accounts by 2027.

data.title: Sweep-in FD vs regular FD: 5 key differences investors should know
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- A sweep-in fixed deposit (FD) is an investment option that helps bank customers earn interest on surplus savings. All the while retaining access to their funds to meet unexpected expenses such as a medical emergency, unforeseen surgery, an accident, or home renovation expenses.

A regular FD, by contrast, permits investors to deposit a lump sum amount for a chosen tenure. Both these investment options can offer better returns than a savings account; still, their liquidity, withdrawal and redemption rules and interest calculations differ.

That is why, before opting to proceed with any of these options, aspiring investors should understand the basic differences between them and compare banks' interest rates, minimum-balance requirements, and premature withdrawal conditions.

A sweep-in FD generally earns the applicable interest rate of a regular FD for the corresponding tenure. However, premature withdrawals may attract penalties or different interest calculations.

For instance, SBI's regular FD rates broadly range from 3.05% to 6.40% p.a., depending on tenure, with sweep-in returns subject to deposit terms. Keeping these basics in mind, let us discuss the core difference between the two. Such an approach will assist aspiring investors with meaningful financial planning.

Note: The salient features and differences discussed above are illustrative. For a complete understanding of specific fixed deposits, refer to the official website of the respective lender.

State Bank of India: Investors can invest in the State Bank of India (SBI) Multi-Option Deposit Scheme (MODS). This scheme supports auto-sweep. Currently, the published minimum auto-sweep threshold is Rs.50,000, with a minimum resulting savings-account balance of Rs.35,000. Deposits under this start as Rs.15,000 in multiples of Rs.5,000, whereas reverse-sweep withdrawals are made in Rs.5,000 units. The rules discussed here are illustrative and subject to change per bank policy. Hence, proper due diligence is a must before considering any investments.

HDFC Bank: Its FD terms specify that premature withdrawals, including sweep-in and partial withdrawals, may attract a 1% reduction in the applicable interest rate. These rules are not fixed; they are tentative and subject to the kind of fixed deposit invested and the bank's policies. Furthermore, linked-account balance requirements and service charges also continue to apply.

ICICI Bank: Effective 5 October 2026, ICICI Bank's fixed deposits (FDs) go up to 6.50% for general customers and 7.10% for senior citizens on eligible tenures. This is a broad range of FD rates and does not guarantee identical effective returns for every sweep-in transaction.

It is essential to keep in mind that sweep-in FDs generally follow the bank's applicable FD rate structure, but actual returns differ when funds are withdrawn early. That is why it is wise to check each bank's current applicable rate card and investment terms before considering any investment.

There cannot be a single answer to this question. As investments are need-based and done according to an individual's financial reality and long-term economic objectives. The investment decision, hence, should be based on how one intends to use their funds.

A sweep-in FD may suit people who want to earn FD interest on surplus funds while retaining convenient access to cash. A regular FD may be more appropriate for money earmarked for a specific goal.

In case of doubt or hesitation, it is wise to seek help from a certified financial advisor before making any investments, as this approach ensures your investments are guided by professionals and made appropriately in line with your long-term financial objectives.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall in Florida — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., Friday night, bringing heavy rains, damaging winds and the possibility of life-threatening flooding to the region.

"Buckle down at this point," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. "Don't be getting out on the roads."

The Category 2 hurricane hit the U.S. Gulf Coast around 9:30 p.m. Eastern time with 105 mph winds, pulling out trees and knocking down power lines before grinding north through Alabama.

More than 700,000 customers in Alabama and Florida were without power early Saturday, according to PowerOutage.com, which tracks outages. Utility companies said they would send out crews to make repairs when it was safe to do so.

"Residents in these areas should have a safe room to ride out the storm and prepare for long-duration power outages," the National Weather Service said.

Forecasters had discontinued storm-surge warnings by 4 a.m. Saturday but said flash, urban and river flooding remained a threat.

As much as 8 inches of rainfall is expected this weekend in southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southwest Georgia, the weather service said.

The hurricane is expected to weaken as it moves inland Saturday, "but Isaias is expected to continue producing gusty winds well inland," the National Weather Service said.

Isaias is the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 in what has been a relatively quiet season.

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO: How Reliance boss Mukesh Ambani's mega issue compares with India's 5 biggest IPOs - price, valuation

Reliance Jio IPO, Oct. 10 -- Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms is preparing for a mega initial public offering (IPO) that could rank among India's largest public issues by fundraising. With a reported price band of Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 per share, the offering is expected to raise up to Rs.30,213 crore and value the company at as much as Rs.10.3 lakh crore, or approximately $106 billion.

With this, Jio IPO is on track to dethrone Hyundai Motor India Limited to become India's largest-ever IPO.

Key dates: The proposed IPO involves up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, with no Offer for Sale (OFS) component from existing institutional shareholders, according to the details provided. The issue is expected to open for anchor investors on October 19, 2026, followed by the public subscription period from October 21 to October 23.

Jio Platforms IPO last recorded Grey Market Premium (GMP) was Rs.172, as on Oct 10, 2026. With a reported upper price band of Rs.1,119, its listing price is estimated to be 1291, indicating a listing premium of 15.4% from IPO price.

Jio Platforms' proposed fundraising puts it alongside some of India's largest IPOs, including Hyundai Motor India, the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Paytm's parent One97 Communications and Tata Capital.

Hyundai Motor India set a record for India's largest IPO when it went public in October 2024. The company launched its issue at a price band of Rs.1,865 to Rs.1,960 per share and raised Rs.27,858.75 crore.

The IPO was entirely an Offer for Sale, allowing Hyundai Motor India's South Korean parent to sell 14.22 crore shares to investors. Unlike Jio Platforms' proposed fresh issue, the Hyundai offering was designed to provide an exit opportunity for the existing shareholder rather than raise fresh capital for the company.

Hyundai Motor India commanded a listing-day market valuation of more than Rs.1.5 lakh crore.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) launched its public issue in September 2026, with a reference price of Rs.1,785 per share and a total issue size of Rs.22,562.71 crore. NSE IPO bidding started from Sep 17, 2026 and ended on Sep 21, 2026.

The offering was structured entirely as an OFS, providing an exit opportunity for existing institutional shareholders while meeting the relevant regulatory requirements. The exchange was valued at approximately $46 billion, placing the issue among India's largest public offerings. The public issue was oversubscribed 4.26 times overall, generating total bids for over 53.80 crore shares against the 12.64 crore shares on offer

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) went public in May 2022 in one of the country's most closely watched divestment exercises. The government offered shares at Rs.902 to Rs.949 apiece and raised Rs.20,557.23 crore by selling a 3.5% stake through an OFS of 22.14 crore shares.

The IPO also included discounts for eligible investors, with retail buyers receiving a Rs.45 discount and policyholders receiving a Rs.60 discount.

The IPO garnered an overall subscription of 2.95 times, with strong participation from policyholders and employees, who were also offered special discounts. The transaction was closely watched globally as it represented one of the largest government-led stake sales in the country's capital market history.

One97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, entered the public markets in November 2021 with an IPO worth Rs.18,300 crore. The issue had a price band of Rs.2,080 to Rs.2,150 per share.

The offering combined a fresh issue of Rs.8,300 crore with an OFS of Rs.10,000 crore. At the upper end of the price band, Paytm's initial market valuation stood at Rs.1.01 lakh crore.

The issue reflected investor interest in India's digital payments and fintech businesses during a period of expansion for the sector. The IPO was subscribed 1.89 times, supported by participation from institutional and retail investors. At the time, it was India's largest-ever IPO and marked a milestone for the country's rapidly expanding fintech sector.

Tata Capital entered the public market in October 2025 with an issue size of Rs.15,511.87 crore. The non-banking financial company used a price cap of Rs.326 per share. The issue was open for subscription from October 6 to October 8, 2025, and the shares were listed on October 13, 2025. data.title: Bitcoin's $19 billion crash still shapes crypto risk a year later
data.description:
One year ago, a single tariff announcement erased more than $19 billion in leveraged crypto bets in about a day. It remains the largest derivatives liquidation episode the market has ever recorded.

The trigger came from Washington, not from inside crypto. President Donald Trump announced a 100% tariff on Chinese imports, and markets that had been priced for good news suddenly had to reprice for a trade war.

Crypto derivatives took the hit fastest. Forced liquidations topped $19 billion across exchanges within a 24-hour window.

The damage reached over 1.6 million accounts. Most of the pain fell on traders betting prices would rise: long positions made up roughly $16–17 billion of the total.

Bitcoin had set an all-time high of nearly $126,200 just four days earlier, on October 6. During the crash, it fell somewhere between 14% and 17% intraday, touching lows in the range of $102,000 to $107,000 before clawing some of it back.

Open interest, the total value of outstanding derivatives contracts, dropped by more than 30% during the selloff. Across the broader crypto market, hundreds of billions in market capitalization vanished within hours.

Binance offered $300 million in compensation to users affected by its automated liquidation process during the volatility.

The crash also exposed structural weak points in how crypto derivatives work. Two stood out: thin liquidity and cross-margin mechanics.

Thin liquidity means there were not enough buyers waiting to absorb the flood of forced selling. Prices gapped down rather than sliding.

Cross-margin is a setup where a trader's whole account balance backs all of their open positions. In a crash, one losing trade can drain collateral that was supporting everything else, turning a single bad bet into a full account wipeout.

On-chain analyses put the realized losses for traders far below $19 billion, with estimates ranging from $950 million to $2.85 billion. The gap exists because the $19 billion reflects the notional size of positions that were closed, not the cash traders actually lost.

Metaplanet reported that its profits fell 39% in Q3, a sign of how the 10/10 event rippled through companies that hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets.

As of early October 2026, Bitcoin trades around $83,000 to $83,500, roughly 34% below its peak.

The liquidation event did flush a large amount of leverage out of the system. But positioning in the months afterward indicated traders had not meaningfully scaled back their appetite for risk. Leverage monitoring around the anniversary shows only modest easing in risk metrics.

For individual traders, the clearest takeaway is about tail risk. The 10/10 crash was set off by a policy announcement from outside the crypto ecosystem. No on-chain metric would have flagged it in advance, and leveraged longs had no time to react before automated systems acted for them.

For exchanges, the episode raised the bar on transparency. Binance's $300 million compensation offer showed that how a platform handles automated liquidations in extreme conditions is a reputational issue, not just a technical one.

A crash that hit over 1.6 million accounts in a single day may push some newcomers toward spot holdings or more conservative strategies, and it could keep others away from derivatives entirely.

Open interest, funding conditions, and the share of positions using cross-margin are the gauges to track. When those climb back toward pre-crash levels while liquidity stays thin, the market is effectively rebuilding the same dominoes that fell on October 10.

data.title: Have leftover money on your forex card after a foreign trip? Here's how to transfer it back to your Indian bank account

data.title: Cohance Lifesciences Appoints Abhimanyu Ojha As CFO
data.description:
Former Intas Pharmaceuticals global CFO takes charge on 12 October as Cohance navigates revenue pressure and planned investments in antibody-drug conjugates

Cohance Lifesciences has appointed Abhimanyu Ojha as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective 12 October 2026, filling the position following Himanshu Agarwal’s departure in September. Ojha brings more than two decades of financial leadership experience in the global healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors, having previously served as Global CFO of Intas Pharmaceuticals.

The appointment comes as Cohance navigates a challenging financial period and pursues investments to expand its capabilities in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), a specialised segment of pharmaceutical development and manufacturing. Ojha’s responsibilities will include overseeing the company’s financial operations and supporting capital allocation decisions as it executes its growth strategy.

Previous CFO Departure

Agarwal resigned from the CFO position in June 2026 and was relieved of his responsibilities on 13 September 2026. Ojha’s appointment formalises the leadership transition at a time when the company is working to strengthen its position in contract development and manufacturing services.

The transition follows the appointment of Umang Vohra, former Cipla chief, as Executive Chairman and Group CEO in April 2026. Vohra assumed the leadership role as Cohance continued to pursue its strategic priorities across complex pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Revenue Faces Pressure

Cohance reported revenue from operations of Rs 422.3 cr in the first quarter of FY27, a year-on-year decline of 23.1%. Gross margins also moderated to 71.5% from 73% in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The financial performance presents a key context for the incoming CFO, particularly in managing operating costs, margins and capital deployment. Future quarterly results will provide a clearer indication of the company’s revenue trajectory and operational performance.

ADC Investment Plans

In September 2026, Cohance announced plans to invest USD 13 million in NJ Bio and USD 5 million in Aruka Bio as part of its strategy to expand its ADC capabilities. The proposed investments are intended to strengthen its presence in specialised pharmaceutical development and manufacturing.

The company’s investment plans place capital allocation and the integration of new capabilities among the financial priorities under its incoming CFO. The execution and returns from these investments will be important considerations as the company expands in higher-value pharmaceutical segments.

Financial Priorities Ahead

Ojha takes charge amid a leadership transition, a decline in quarterly revenue and planned investments in specialised manufacturing capabilities. His experience in pharmaceutical finance will be relevant as Cohance balances expansion plans with operating performance and financial discipline.

The company’s subsequent financial results and progress on its investment commitments will help indicate how effectively it converts its strategic plans into sustainable business performance.

data.title: Alok Industries Exits Czech Textile Subsidiary Mileta In Rs 5.6 Cr Deal
data.description:
The divestment follows a December 2025 agreement with CRESCON and removes Mileta from Alok Industries’ subsidiary structure

Alok Industries has completed the sale of its entire stake in Czech textile manufacturer Mileta a.s. for EUR 558,825, equivalent to approximately Rs 5.6 crore. The company informed the stock exchanges on 9 October 2026 that Alok Industries International Limited, its step-down wholly owned subsidiary, had completed the transaction.

The sale follows a share purchase agreement signed on 16 December 2025 between Alok Industries International Limited and CRESCON a.s., a company incorporated in the Czech Republic.

Under the agreement, the subsidiary agreed to transfer its entire equity stake in Mileta to CRESCON. The December filing stated that the transaction was subject to customary closing conditions and that Mileta would cease to be a subsidiary of Alok Industries upon completion.

The latest disclosure confirms that the transaction has closed. CRESCON operates in residential and resort property development and does not belong to Alok Industries’ promoter group or group companies, according to the original filing.

Mileta's Financial Performance

Mileta manufactures textile fibres, fabrics and other textile products. Its operations also include yarn dyeing, chemical processing of fabrics and wholesale trade. The company operates facilities in Horice, which handles weaving and administration, and Cerny Dul, which undertakes processing activities in the Czech Republic.

Mileta contributed approximately 4.11 per cent to Alok Industries’ consolidated turnover in FY25, according to the December 2025 disclosure. The company reported sales of Rs 152.27 crore and a loss of Rs 49.63 crore for the year ended 31 March 2025, compared with sales of Rs 153.23 crore and a loss of Rs 28.53 crore in FY24.

Alok Industries’ FY26 annual report information shows that Mileta’s sales increased to Rs 189.62 crore, while its loss narrowed to Rs 5.92 crore. The figures indicate an improvement in the subsidiary’s reported financial performance before the completion of the divestment. However, the disclosures reviewed do not establish the reasons behind the sale or quantify its impact on Alok Industries’ future profitability and debt position.

Sale Ends Subsidiary Status

The transaction transfers Alok Industries International Limited’s entire equity stake in Mileta to CRESCON. With the sale complete, Mileta no longer forms part of Alok Industries’ subsidiary structure. The company’s disclosures confirm the transaction value and completion but do not specify how Alok Industries intends to use the proceeds. The effect of the disposal on the group’s consolidated financial position will depend on the accounting treatment and any related costs or adjustments.

data.title: S&P 500 at 10,000 or bust: New ETF offers investors all-or-nothing bet on the index
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

A new ETF is a long-term leveraged bet on the popular stock index

It's becoming harder to draw the line between investing and gambling.

Wall Street has continued to blur the lines between investing and gambling with one recently launched exchange-traded fund.

Earlier this month, Roundhill Investments launched the Roundhill S&P 500 Target 10,000 2030 ETF XX. The ETF essentially offers investors the chance to take a long-term leveraged bet that the S&P 500 SPX will continue to climb.

Options contracts held by the fund may deliver a substantial payout if the S&P 500 is trading above 10,000 on Jan. 10, 2030, when the contracts expire.

If the index falls short, then the contracts will expire worthless. Although the outcome for the options is binary, investors don't necessarily need to hold the fund until the contracts expire.

ETFs that use derivatives like options to offer investors leveraged exposure to a given index, stock or asset have proliferated in recent years. But, as Roundhill CEO Dave Mazza pointed out, most of these products have catered to day traders, by employing leverage that resets daily.

Unlike the hundreds of leveraged and inverse ETFs that came before it, the new Roundhill ETF is designed as a long-term leveraged play on the direction of the S&P 500.

With the S&P 500 notching a new record high earlier this week after three straight years of double-digit gains, a target of just above 10,000 probably appears within reach to many. Achieving the target would require a compound annual growth rate of about 8%, according to MarketWatch calculations.

That's slightly higher than the long-term average: Going back to 1928, the S&P 500 has delivered a compounded price return of 6.4%, excluding dividends, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Like prediction markets, the fund offers investors the chance to take a "binary bet" on a predetermined outcome, said Dave Nadig, president and director of research at ETF.com, in an interview. That's where the gambling aspect comes into play, he noted. But because the leverage is long term and the product is packaged in an ETF, it might seem less risky to potential buyers.

"It's a bizarre way to think about the markets. It's gamification," Nadig said.

How it works

Instead of using binary prediction-market contracts, the ETF will invest in leaps, or long-term equity anticipation securities. These are long-dated options contracts - a kind of long-term portfolio insurance that can also be used to speculate.

Shares of the Roundhill ETF should rise and fall based on the value of the option contracts that it holds. These contracts are linked to an ETF that tracks the S&P 500. As the S&P 500 rises toward 10,000, the value of these contracts will likely increase, along with their likelihood of delivering a payoff.

At the same time, the contracts will lose some of their value as time passes and their expiration dates approach. For longer-dated options, the process of time decay happens slowly. Time to expiration and the volatility of the underlying stock index are dynamics that will drive price action in the ETF.

As for how much investors should expect the ETF to move from day to day, Drew Pettit, CIO at Roundhill Investments, said the contracts currently leave the ETF with 5.5 times embedded leverage to the S&P 500.

The fund's early performance offers a more concrete picture. On Oct. 2, when the S&P 500 rose 0.7%, the ETF rose 7.4%. When the index fell by 0.5% on Thursday, the ETF fell 4.9%, FactSet data showed.

To reach 10,000, the S&P 500 would have to climb almost 29% from Thursday's closing level. Whether it gets there or not, the ride will likely be a bumpy one.

"This is a volatile investment," said Roundhill's Mazza. "For someone who is just looking for long-term equity-market returns, this strategy is not for them."

Akin to gambling

Leveraged ETFs are generally risky and take big swings. Still, they have exploded in number over the past couple years. Meanwhile, a growing number of more speculative products have helped to inspire a flurry of new ETF launches.

"From a cultural and marketing standpoint," much of the ETF industry's product development over the last year has been "highly speculative" or akin to gambling, Nadig said.

"People are actually trying to wedge gambling into every corner of the financial market right now," he said. "I'm very, very against using the financial markets to create binary speculative bets."

The value of an option is not just a function of its time to expiration, but also factors in the volatility of the underlying product and how close it is to the strike price, said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers.

"The trick to options trading is, did the underlying move happen quickly enough to defeat your decay," Sosnick said.

During the years before the contracts it is holding expire, the Roundhill ETF's structure and volatility profile will likely attract day traders looking to make short-term bets on the S&P 500.

Investors also have the option of buying the long-dated options contracts themselves - but that would involve paying up-front premiums to buy the contracts, which could carry wide spreads, and ETFs offer a potentially more palatable vehicle. The long-term nature of the leverage will also spare traders from the intense volatility decay experienced from holding leveraged ETFs that see big price swings and that reset daily.

Michael DeStefano contributed.

-Christine Idzelis

data.title: Is Your Grown Child Pulling Away? These Are the Early Signs of Estrangement — WSJ
data.description:
By Elizabeth Bernstein

When I interview parents who are estranged from their adult children, many say: "My child cut me off out of the blue. I didn't see it coming."

Yet people who have gone "no contact" with their parents often tell me that this decision was their last resort — and a long time coming.

Why the disconnect?

Estrangement typically occurs on a continuum — and parents don't always recognize the signs, says Kristina Scharp, a communication professor at Rutgers University who studies the issue. Think of a scale from one to 10, where 10 is full contact between parent and child and one is none. In between, there is a slow pullback: fewer calls and visits, less access granted.

"It's a myth that estrangement is always all or nothing," Scharp says.

Scharp identified eight characteristics of estrangement, or areas in which adult children who are pulling away from their parents change their behaviors or feelings:

Communication quantity: They reduce the amount of contact. In a less-severe estrangement, they might call from time to time. In a more severe case, there is no contact.

Communication quality: They stop sharing meaningful or personal information. Instead of talking about their job or partner, for example, they might talk about the weather.

Physical distance: They move away or stay away. Some might remain in touch. Others move and don't tell their parents where they live.

Presence or absence of emotion: The amount of emotion that they feel for their parent changes. Some are flooded with anger or devastation. Others report feeling numb.

Positive or negative affect: The flavor of emotion changes, often becoming more negative as the child becomes more estranged. For example, someone might go from feeling that their mom is difficult to resenting or even hating her.

Desire for reconciliation: The wish to remain in the family changes. Some decide to cut ties. Others hold out hope that the relationship can be repaired if certain parental behaviors change.

Role reciprocity: They no longer think their parents are behaving the way a mom and dad should. And they stop behaving as a child might be expected to toward a parent. For instance, they may refuse to visit when a parent is sick or even dying.

Legal action: They formally sever ties with a parent, like changing their name or beneficiaries in their will.

All of these behaviors occur on a spectrum, and not all are at play in every estrangement, Scharp says. People may also fluctuate, moving closer — or away — from a parent at different times.

If parents understand this, they may be able to improve the relationship. "The continuum is where the compromise can exist," Scharp says.

On Reddit, commenters share strategies on how to pull back from parents: respond to every other call or text; return calls when you know your parents will be busy; request that they stop asking about you; and start "grey rocking," which is to deliberately make your communication as dull and unresponsive as, well, a grey rock.

Yet people who are pulling away don't always tell their parents. Even when they do, parents sometimes resist the boundaries their children are trying to set.

Meanwhile, parents may mistake the pullback as a natural developmental phase, realizing the scope only in hindsight.

"The final cutoff is the undeniable writing on the wall," says Jennifer Hershon, a family-estrangement coach based in Sacramento. "But there's room for repair before the pattern is entrenched."

Joe Bernstein, 51, spent decades trying to set boundaries with his dad after what he described as an adverse childhood. First, he tried talking to his father less. Then when he got married and had a child, he stopped sharing news of his family and refused to allow get-togethers. He also tried to actively put his dad out of his mind.

But none of this made him feel better, Bernstein says. He still had flashbacks about incidents in his childhood. He felt consumed by anger. And the more he pulled away, the more his father pushed back, he says.

Then three years ago, Bernstein started therapy, which helped him process his feelings. When his dad later criticized this, Bernstein says he responded by blocking his father.

"This gives me the quantum of solace to step back and sit more peacefully with the situation," says Bernstein, a higher-education administrator in Chicago. "And it leads to even a sense of compassion for him because he had a rough childhood, too."

As for a potential reconciliation, Bernstein says he would welcome it if his father was able to treat him with respect and civility. "That would be the better outcome," he says. "Because ending things in darkness isn't good for anyone."

What can estranged parents and children do to bridge the divide?

Not all people who have pulled away or cut off a parent may want to reconnect. If they were abused, for example, it may be safer to stay away.

Yet many estrangements are caused by communication or boundary issues. In these instances, therapists recommend parents and kids who want to repair the relationship meet in a neutral setting, like a restaurant, to talk. The adult child should acknowledge that they are pulling away — and focus on patterns, not individual incidents, when they explain what is wrong.

Parents should have a notebook with them, says Catherine Hickem, a psychotherapist in Atlanta who specializes in parent-adult child relationships. She recommends that parents tell their child: "I realize I have made some mistakes that have hurt you and I want to hear about all of them."

It is important for parents not to be defensive, try to explain themselves or justify their actions, Hickem says. They should listen. Tell their child that they appreciate the courage it took to tell the truth. And promise to work to change their behavior.

Then the parent should take a few days to reflect on what they heard, call their child back and keep the dialogue going.

"Repair is not this fully cathartic moment," says Rachel Haack, a licensed marriage and family therapist in Reno, Nev., who works with families dealing with estrangement. "It's staying connected through the distance."

Write to Elizabeth Bernstein at Elizabeth.Bernstein@wsj.com

Avenue Supermarts, which operates DMart stores, reported an 8.5% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹743.5 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 (Q2 FY27), against ₹685 crore a year earlier, the company said on 10 October 2026.

Consolidated revenue rose 17.8% to ₹19,644 crore from ₹16,676 crore. EBITDA grew 15% to ₹1,394 crore from ₹1,214 crore. The margin was 7%, against 7.3% a year ago.

On a standalone basis, net profit rose 7.6% to ₹803.5 crore from ₹746.5 crore. Revenue grew 18.4% to ₹19,206 crore from ₹16,219 crore, and EBITDA rose 14% to ₹1,403 crore from ₹1,230 crore. The margin was 7%, against 7.6% a year ago. Standalone basic earnings per share (EPS) stood at ₹12.32, against ₹11.47.

For the half year ended 30 September 2026 (H1 FY27), standalone revenue grew 16.8% to ₹37,550 crore. EBITDA rose 15.2% to ₹2,930 crore, and net profit increased 10.3% to ₹1,739 crore. Standalone basic EPS was ₹26.67, against ₹24.22.

Consolidated half-year revenue stood at ₹38,439 crore, against ₹33,036 crore a year earlier. Consolidated EBITDA was ₹2,892 crore, against ₹2,513 crore, and net profit was ₹1,603 crore, against ₹1,458 crore.

Commenting on the DMart brick-and-mortar business, Managing Director and CEO Anshul Asawa said stores that are two years and older grew 9.5% in Q2 FY27, against 6.8% in Q2 FY26. He said the pricing proposition remains strong in an inflationary environment, while wage inflation at entry level has led to a marginal increase in operating expenses.

The company opened 15 new stores during the quarter, taking its total store count to 518. This includes one store at Navi Mumbai that is currently closed for customers due to reconstruction. The company added 18 stores in H1 FY27. As of 30 September 2026, the stores had a retail business area of 21.4 million sq ft.

Vikram Dasu, whole-time director and CEO of Avenue E-Commerce, said on the DMart Ready business that the company is focused on driving greater operational efficiencies and strengthening customer experience in the cities where it currently operates.

On the NSE, Avenue Supermarts shares closed at ₹3,516.80, down ₹68.20, or 1.90%.

data.title: China proposes stricter car design, testing rules, including ban on fully hidden door handles
data.description:
China's industry ministry on Saturday proposed tighter oversight of automakers' innovative designs and research and development testing. It said some manufacturers had rushed out new models without enough validation, which raised safety and environmental risks.

• From January 1, 2027, automakers seeking approval for new models must submit more technical details on innovative designs and testing. Models that are poorly tested or backed by false data will be rejected, the draft said

• Models that already have approval must file information on their innovative designs by July 1, 2027. If they do not and have safety hazards, automakers must halt production and recall them

• The draft bans fully hidden door handles and foldable or flexible displays. It also bars use of "zero-gravity" or swivel seats while driving

• Key functions such as lights and wipers must keep physical controls

• The ministry drafted the rules with three other agencies and is taking public comment until November 10

data.title: Adani Green Energy capacity rises 24% in April-September, energy sales up 32%
data.description:
Adani Green Energy's operational renewable energy capacity increased 24% year-on-year to 20,763 MW in the first half of FY27, while energy sales rose 32% to 25,747 million units, according to the company's provisional operational update released on October 10.

The company added 4,083 MW of greenfield capacity during the April-September period. Of this, 621 MW was added during the second quarter of FY27.

The company also operationalised 3,081 MWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity at Khavda in Gujarat during the July-September quarter, taking its total installed BESS capacity to 6,632 MWh as of September 30, 2026.

Adani Green Energy reported a capacity utilisation factor (CUF) of 22.9% for its solar portfolio, 42.9% for its wind portfolio and 45.2% for its hybrid portfolio during H1 FY27. Plant availability stood at 99.3% for solar, 94.6% for wind and 98.8% for hybrid projects.

The company said its operational portfolio powered more than 4.4 million homes and helped avoid 17.5 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions during the first half of FY27.

The operational update is provisional and covers the six months ended September 30, 2026.
